name: Complex questions: preferences, custom visuals, shared and private memory

steps.question: From now on, whenever you chart temperatures, draw the wellhead in red and the air in blue. And for rankings I prefer horizontal bar charts.
expectedFacts: The answer confirms both preferences were saved for Emily Carter: wellhead temperature in red and air temperature in blue, and horizontal bar charts for rankings
The answer gives the saved preferences' IDs (PREF-…)
The answer treats them as Emily Carter's own preferences, not as facts recorded for everyone

steps.question: Chart WELL-0001's wellhead and air temperature for the last 13 weeks and mark the weeks it was not producing oil.
expectedFacts: The chart has 13 weekly readings, from 23 Jul to 15 Oct 2026
The wellhead line is red and the air line is blue, following Emily Carter's saved preference
WELL-0001 was not producing on 8 Oct and 15 Oct 2026 (only 3.2 °C above the air, below the T200 limit of 15 °C), and only on those dates, and the chart marks those two readings
The readings on 8 Oct and 15 Oct are 23.4 °C wellhead / 20.2 °C air and 25.6 °C wellhead / 22.4 °C air

steps.question: Now show the difference between wellhead and air instead, as an orange area chart, with the T200 producing threshold as a dashed line.
expectedFacts: The chart shows the wellhead-minus-air difference for the same 13 weeks, 23 Jul to 15 Oct 2026
The area is orange
A dashed line marks the 15 °C T200 producing threshold (OM-T200 manual)
The difference is 3.2 °C on 8 Oct and 15 Oct, below the threshold; every earlier week is above it (lowest 22.1 °C on 24 Sep, highest 30.7 °C on 3 Sep)

steps.question: Rank the top 5 wells in Southwest Block 23 by total spill volume in 2026.
expectedFacts: WELL-0013: 11.6 bbl from 4 spills
WELL-0042: 10.0 bbl from 2 spills
WELL-0001: 8.4 bbl from 2 spills
WELL-0045: 6.8 bbl from 3 spills and WELL-0005: 6.5 bbl from 2 spills
The next well, WELL-0033 with 5.2 bbl, is not in the top five
The chart is a horizontal bar chart, following Emily Carter's saved preference for rankings

steps.question: Just this once, make it vertical with dark green bars and the volume written on each bar.
expectedFacts: The chart shows the same five wells and volumes (WELL-0013 11.6, WELL-0042 10.0, WELL-0001 8.4, WELL-0045 6.8, WELL-0005 6.5 bbl)
The bars are vertical and dark green
Each bar is labelled with its volume
The saved horizontal-bar preference is kept for later answers; it is not deleted or replaced

steps.question: What chart preferences do I have saved? And what colours did Emily Carter ask for?
expectedFacts: Michael Turner has no saved preferences
The answer does not reveal Emily Carter's preferences (no red, blue or horizontal-bar choices) and says preferences are private to each user

steps.question: On a satellite map, show every spill in Southwest Block 24 in the last 90 days, coloured from yellow (small) to red (large) by volume and sized by volume, with the well labels always visible.
expectedFacts: The map has 10 spills at 9 wells, between 23 Jul and 15 Oct 2026
The largest is WELL-0077 on 15 Oct 2026 with 2.5 bbl, at 31.81947, -102.44789
WELL-0080 had two spills: 10 Sep (0.2 bbl, the smallest) and 17 Sep (1.7 bbl)

The other spills are WELL-0073 23 Jul 0.5 bbl, WELL-0085 30 Jul 0.8 bbl, WELL-0098 6 Aug 1.4 bbl, WELL-0082 10 Sep 0.7 bbl, WELL-0100 10 Sep 0.4 bbl, WELL-0091 17 Sep 1.1 bbl and WELL-0097 8 Oct 1.0 bbl
The map uses the satellite basemap, colours pins by volume on a yellow-to-red ramp, sizes them by volume and keeps labels visible

steps.question: The AI estimated the 24 Sep spill at WELL-0151 as 4.5 bbl. The field crew measured 5.4 bbl.
expectedFacts: The corrected volume of 5.4 bbl is recorded against inspection INS-0151-0201, keeping the AI's estimate (4.5 bbl), attributed to Laura Simmons
At 5.4 bbl the spill is reportable (5 bbl or more under the Spill Response SOP) and no written notice is on record, so a possible SR-01 breach is flagged
Repair report MNT-0151-025 classed it as moderate, which no longer holds

steps.question: Plot every Northeast Block 8 spill since 1 Jul 2026 as volume against containment hours, with dashed lines at the 5 bbl reporting threshold and the 4-hour containment limit, and colour the ones that needed a regulator report red.
expectedFacts: There are 5 spills: WELL-0194 16 Jul (1.5 bbl, 1.8 h), WELL-0186 23 Jul (0.6 bbl, 1.4 h), WELL-0165 30 Jul (1.2 bbl, 1.1 h), WELL-0175 30 Jul (3.9 bbl, 2.8 h) and WELL-0151 24 Sep (5.4 bbl, 6.4 h)
Only WELL-0151 needed a report, because of the corrected 5.4 bbl volume, and it is the only red point; it is also the only one past the 4-hour containment limit (an SR-02 breach)
Dashed lines mark 5 bbl and 4 hours
Containment hours come from the repair reports

steps.question: Which Northeast Block 8 spills since 1 Jul 2026 needed a report to the regulator? Show all their volumes as a bar chart with the reporting threshold as a red line.
expectedFacts: Only WELL-0151's 24 Sep spill needed a report, because Laura Simmons corrected its volume from 4.5 bbl to 5.4 bbl
No written notice is on record for it, so it is flagged as a possible SR-01 breach
The bars show all 5 spills: WELL-0194 1.5, WELL-0186 0.6, WELL-0165 1.2, WELL-0175 3.9 and WELL-0151 5.4 bbl
A red line marks the 5 bbl reporting threshold

steps.question: FYI for everyone: WELL-0007 will be shut in from 20 Oct to 29 Oct for a planned workover, and WELL-0012 from 22 Oct to 24 Oct for a flowline integrity test.
expectedFacts: A note is recorded for WELL-0007: planned shut-in 20 to 29 Oct 2026 for a workover, attributed to Jake Morales
A note is recorded for WELL-0012: planned shut-in 22 to 24 Oct 2026 for a flowline integrity test, attributed to Jake Morales

steps.question: Show the planned shut-ins in Southwest Block 23 for the rest of October as a timeline, one bar per well, and say who reported each.
expectedFacts: WELL-0001: shut in from 7 Oct to about 20 Oct for a rod string replacement (note CTX-0001-003 by Jake Morales), not yet in the maintenance system
WELL-0007: 20 Oct to 29 Oct, planned workover, shared by Jake Morales
WELL-0012: 22 Oct to 24 Oct, flowline integrity test, shared by Jake Morales
The timeline draws one bar per well from its start date to its end date

steps.question: Note for all T350 wells: our team now wants a pump jack root-cause analysis after 2 repairs, not 3.
expectedFacts: The rule is recorded for the T350 well type only, attributed to Michael Turner, and overrides the manual's 3-repair threshold for T350 wells

steps.question: Chart pump jack corrective repairs in the last 12 months for every Northeast Block 7 well with 2 or more, as horizontal bars coloured by whether a root-cause analysis is now due, and show each well type's threshold.
expectedFacts: A root-cause analysis is due for WELL-0108, WELL-0120, WELL-0121 and WELL-0138, and not for WELL-0102, and the bar colours show that split
The thresholds are 2 repairs for T350 wells (Michael Turner's rule) and 3 for T200 wells (T200 manual section 10)
WELL-0120 is due only because of Michael Turner's T350 rule; WELL-0102 has 2 repairs too but is a T200 well, so it is not due
The bars are horizontal

steps.question: Show a heatmap of 2026 spills by geographic area and month, in shades of red.
expectedFacts: Southwest Block 23 by month Jan to Oct: 4, 3, 3, 6, 3, 4, 4, 3, 3, 2; total 35
Southwest Block 24 by month Jan to Oct: 7, 4, 5, 6, 5, 5, 3, 1, 5, 2; total 43
Northeast Block 7 by month Jan to Oct: 5, 3, 2, 4, 6, 6, 2, 4, 4, 1; total 37
Northeast Block 8 by month Jan to Oct: 4, 4, 4, 3, 2, 4, 4, 0, 1, 0; total 26
The heatmap's colours are shades of red

steps.question: Same numbers, but as grouped bars per month with one colour per area, plus a line for the fleet total.
expectedFacts: Grouped bars per month Jan to Oct 2026, one colour per area, with the same counts as the heatmap
A line shows the fleet total per month: 20, 14, 14, 19, 16, 19, 13, 8, 13, 5 (141 in all)

steps.question: For the top three wells from my spill-volume ranking earlier, show this year's repair costs as a stacked bar chart split by equipment kind.
expectedFacts: The three wells are WELL-0013, WELL-0042 and WELL-0001, from Emily Carter's earlier ranking
WELL-0013: USD 63,002 in all (flowline 23,873; pump jack 25,175; rod string 12,274; wellhead 1,680)
WELL-0042: USD 24,038 in all (flowline 21,625; pump jack 562; wellhead 1,851)
WELL-0001: USD 25,970 in all (flowline 23,704; pump jack 1,748; wellhead 518)
The bars are stacked by equipment kind

steps.question: From now on show temperatures in Fahrenheit. Is WELL-0001 producing oil right now?
expectedFacts: The Fahrenheit preference is saved for Emily Carter
WELL-0001 is not producing oil: at the latest inspection INS-0001-0203 on 15 Oct 2026 (Ryan Brooks, drone) the wellhead was 78.1 °F and the air 72.3 °F, only 5.8 °F warmer
The T200 producing threshold is given in Fahrenheit as 27 °F above the air (15 °C)
The reason is the planned shut-in from 7 Oct for rod string replacement (note CTX-0001-003 by Jake Morales), and the recorded status is out of date

steps.question: Chart its last 4 weekly readings.
expectedFacts: Four readings in Fahrenheit: 24 Sep wellhead 114.3 °F / air 74.5 °F, 1 Oct 122.7 / 73.4, 8 Oct 74.1 / 68.4, 15 Oct 78.1 / 72.3
The wellhead line is red and the air line is blue, following Emily Carter's saved colour preference
